copy.title: The LeBron James Money File
copy.desc: An interactive, fully sourced map of LeBron James’s family: who owns what, whether you can buy into their companies, the homes, and the money on the public record.
copy.eyebrow: File #023 · The James family · Data as of
copy.h1: The first active NBA billionaire has a family. We followed the money.
copy.lede: Who’s who, what each of them owns, whether you can buy stock in their companies, the homes, and the money on the public record. Every number links to its source.
copy.familyLede: Tap anyone to open their file: what they own, what’s on the record, and where every fact comes from. The kids are listed by first name only.
copy.investLede: None of these companies trade on the stock market. Most are privately owned, and Beats was sold to Apple in 2014.
copy.moneyLede: Forbes counts more than $500 million in NBA salary and more than $1 billion earned off the court. LeBron is the only one in the family with a published net worth.
copy.homesLede: Forbes counted at least three properties in 2022. Prices are what he paid, as Forbes reported them. No street addresses here.
copy.recordLede: The money that shows up in contracts, deals and company announcements. Reporting and records, not guesses.
copy.trailLede: From Akron in 1984 to the first billionaire still playing in the NBA.
copy.calcYearsK: Years to earn what LeBron has

summary.t: The NBA’s career scoring leader and, per Forbes, the first active NBA player to become a billionaire. After eight seasons with the Lakers, he signed with the Philadelphia 76ers in July 2026.

owns.t: Got a minority stake in Liverpool F.C. in 2011, when his sports marketing business partnered with Fenway Sports Group. In 2021 he and Maverick Carter swapped their Liverpool stakes for part ownership of FSG. Forbes estimated his share at about 1% in 2022.

His production company. A 2021 sale of a minority stake valued it at $725 million; Forbes said he was the largest single shareholder, with a stake believed to be under 50%. In November 2024 it agreed to merge with Fulwell 73.

Paid less than $1 million for a 10% stake in 2012. Forbes valued it at about $30 million in 2022. He passed on a McDonald’s endorsement, worth an estimated $15 million over four years, to promote Blaze.
Owned a small slice of Beats when Apple bought it for $3 billion in 2014.

record.t: Signed a lifetime deal with Nike in late 2015. His business manager, Maverick Carter, said it would pay out at least $1 billion. Forbes says it pays him tens of millions of dollars a year.

Signed a two-year, $97.1 million extension in August 2022, then re-signed in July 2024 for two years and $104 million, with a player option in the second year. Forbes noted in October 2025 that he was in the last year of that deal.
In July 2026 he agreed to a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers, with a player option, ending an eight-year run with the Lakers.
Forbes counts more than $500 million in NBA salary and more than $1 billion, before taxes, from business off the court.
His family foundation opened its first elementary school in 2018 and has pledged more than $40 million for college funding.

facts.t: Forbes declared him a billionaire in June 2022, the first active NBA player to reach that mark.
He and Bronny became the first father and son to play in an NBA game together, on October 22, 2024, and the first to play together in a playoff game, in April 2026.
Forbes estimated he would earn $124.5 million in the 2022–23 season, before taxes and agent fees.

kidsNote.t: LeBron and Savannah have three children, listed here by first name only; the oldest, Bronny, plays for the Lakers on a four-year, $7.9 million deal signed in 2024.

summary.t: LeBron’s high school sweetheart from Akron. They married on September 14, 2013, in San Diego. She launched the skincare brand Reframe Beauty in 2025.

worth.none: No reliable public estimate of her own.

owns.t: Her skincare brand, launched in 2025 with Nick Axelrod-Welk.

facts.t: Owned a juice store, The Juice Spot, in Miami’s Brickell area. It closed in 2016 after the family moved back to Ohio.
In 2010 she and LeBron released Home Court, a children’s bedroom furniture line with American Signature.
Launched the podcast Everybody’s Crazy with April McDaniel in April 2024, and founded the mentorship program Women of Our Future.

summary.t: Was 16 when LeBron was born in Akron. They moved between apartments while she looked for steady work, and she later let him live with the family of Frank Walker, a youth football coach who introduced him to basketball.

record.t: For his 18th birthday she gave him a Hummer H2, bought with a loan she secured on his future earning power as an NBA player.

companies.name: Fenway Sports Group
companies.t: Owns baseball, soccer and hockey teams, including the Boston Red Sox and Liverpool F.C. Privately held, so there’s no stock to buy.

companies.name: The SpringHill Company
companies.t: His production company. RedBird, Fenway Sports Group, Nike and Epic Games invested at a $725 million valuation in 2021. Agreed in November 2024 to merge with Fulwell 73, the producer of The Kardashians.

companies.name: Blaze Pizza
companies.t: Fast-casual pizza chain with more than 300 company-owned and franchised stores in 2022. Forbes valued his stake at about $30 million that year.

companies.name: Beats by Dre
companies.t: Apple bought Beats for $3 billion in 2014. LeBron owned a small slice.

props.name: 1930s hilltop house
props.note: He tore it down to build a mansion of his own.

summary.note: Forbes’s June 2022 count: at least three properties, worth about $80 million in all, including a mansion he built near Akron.

extra.t: He built a $10 million mansion near his hometown of Akron, Ohio.
